subject: snail
pitch: A garden snail on an adventure. A glossy spiral shell striped in caramel, chocolate and cream, a soft grey-green body with a pebbly texture and a slimy shine, two long eye stalks with little black eyes and two short feelers below. A tiny ladybird hitches a ride on top of the shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning a simple snail model with limited SDK knowledge, sketching out a small-scale skeleton starting with a root joint and rough body/shell dimensions.

For the body I'll use named joints with parent relationships to build a chain from tail to head, then attach flattened sphere parts to approximate the segmented body and foot shape. For the shell, I'm considering building it from spheres placed along a spiral path of growing radius to mimic the coiled snail shell shape.

Planning the shell stripes now: instead of coloring spheres sequentially along the spiral (which would create rings crossing the tube), I'll place three smaller offset spheres per spiral step in cream, chocolate, and caramel so the color bands run lengthwise along the coil, giving it a realistic striped appearance with around a hundred spheres total for a dense, smooth spiral.

Checking the proportions, my initial growth rate made the shell way too large relative to the body, so I'm scaling down the spiral's base radius and growth constant to get something closer to a realistic garden snail shell size, around 1.5cm end radius.

Now I'm working out tube thickness and stripe positioning along the shell, keeping the x-position centered, and planning to place a small ladybird decoration at the very top of the spiral by tracking the maximum height reached as I build each sphere.

I'm designing the ladybird itself with a red dome body, black head, spots, a back line, tiny legs and antennae, then figuring out the spiral's heading direction and where the body joints (root, tail, foot) should sit relative to the shell.

Now I'm working on the slug-like body: a sequence of flattened spheres forming the segmented body, a bigger hump ellipsoid underneath the shell, and a raised neck leading to the head sphere. I'm also figuring out how to build the eye stalks using small jointed parts, aiming cylinders along a direction between two points since the exact API for orienting rod-like parts isn't fully clear yet.

Next I'm detailing the stalks as three tapering segments splayed outward with a black eyeball sphere and tiny white highlight at the tip, plus short feelers near the mouth with little tip bulbs, and I'm starting on the jaw parts for the mouth along with the pebbly skin texture.

Adding body bumps...

Now I'm working out the width taper function along the body, then setting up the skeleton: a root hips joint with a parent chain branching to tail segments, chest, and head, each positioned along the spine at specific z-coordinates.

I'll compute yc so the sphere bottom sits near ground level, then build an ellipsoid helper by baking scale into a base sphere geometry since I'm unsure how scale options are accepted directly. I'll keep colors minimal and attach parts to bones via an "at" position plus bone reference, with directional rotation for cylinder-shaped limbs.

Now I'm adding a ladybird: a red ellipsoid body, a small black head, black spots positioned on the dome using spherical offset math, a thin center line, and legs attached to its own joint under the shell.

Then I'm positioning the shell's spiral and color scheme—caramel, chocolate, cream—along with the apex and tracking the max top height to place the ladybird correctly on the curved surface.

Working out the cross-striping of the layers: a cream sphere in the center, chocolate ones offset to either side, and smaller caramel ones further out, repeated along the spiral path for a symmetrical candy-twist look. That gives roughly 200 small spheres total, keeping the shell's width around 0.026 units.

I'm now mapping the tail and body segments to z-position ranges, defining which "bone" (tail sections, hips, chest, head) each z-coordinate belongs to so each part can be placed and shaped correctly, with the head starting at its own sphere placement.

Now I'm building out the head details: computing the rising neck/head y-position curve, sizing the head sphere, and positioning the eye stalks as two-segment bent appendages with small eye spheres at the tips, colored slightly darker than the body.

I'm also placing the feelers near the mouth, setting up the upper/lower jaw boxes as a hinged mouth with a dark lip line, and refining the body/belly/foot color palette toward soft grey-greens.

Now I'm writing a helper function to build cylinder-based limb segments between two points, computing direction and length so the geometry orients correctly between joints.
